title: The Man Who Saved the World
lines: In {1983~nineteen eighty-three}, one man stopped a nuclear war | by refusing to believe a computer.
September twenty-sixth. A secret bunker near Moscow. | Just after midnight. | Three weeks earlier, the Soviets had shot down a passenger jet. Tension is at its peak.
The alarm goes off: a US missile launch. | Then another. | Five in total. | The computer rates it: high reliability.
Stanislav Petrov has minutes to report it. | A report could trigger a counterstrike, | and a full nuclear war.
But a real attack would be hundreds of missiles, not five. | And the ground {radar/~radar} sees nothing.
He calls it a false alarm. | And waits. | Twenty-three minutes later, nothing has happened.
He was right. | Sunlight on high {clouds/~clouds} had fooled the satellites. | The story stayed secret for fifteen years.
Would you have trusted the computer? | Tell me in the comments.
